results.name: Seoul
results.key_finding: Seoul runs a genuinely strong, well-funded anticipatory welfare programme (451.3bn won, five years, against loneliness and lonely deaths) but the 2026-09-21 national audit finding shows its own procurement-integrity controls did not catch a division director monetising a 1.04bn-won contract for a year.

results.name: Columbia University
results.key_finding: Two federal agencies found in May 2025 that Columbia acted with deliberate indifference to harassment of Jewish students over 19 months, and Columbia then paid 221 million dollars and accepted externally set discipline rules to restore its funding — a pattern of correcting only under compulsion that the published Functional rating does not reflect.

results.name: El Salvador
results.key_finding: The expiry of Temporary Protected Status for roughly 200,000 Salvadorans is a United States decision and is not scored against El Salvador; what is scoreable is El Salvador’s own silence, and that is already priced into a near-floor score set in July 2026 on the government’s own conduct.

results.name: Anthropic
results.key_finding: A researcher resigned and warned publicly about catastrophic AI risk, and Anthropic’s own alignment lead publicly agreed with him — but an individual’s speech is not institutional conduct, and the one arguably institutional element (a senior employee conceding the company has no plan) is already reflected in the SYS score of 3.0 carried from 15 September.

results.name: Thailand
results.key_finding: Thailand’s local-government exam scandal is evidence of systemic corruption in public appointments and of state machinery working against it at the same time: police have seized 320.86 million baht and the Interior Ministry has ordered a check of all 480,000 papers, but nothing is yet adjudicated.

results.name: Amsterdam
results.key_finding: Amsterdam is unusually honest about its own failures — it let outside researchers document a discriminatory city algorithm and then scrapped it, and its mayor publicly says the city is buckling — but its independent ombudsman finds vulnerable residents still stuck in rules and waiting times, which does not support an Exemplary rating.

results.name: Georgia
results.key_finding: The ICE raid that detained 475 people at the Hyundai plant was federal conduct and the 15 September 2026 claim is against the United States, not Georgia; the state’s own documented response was to protect the investment relationship, which is consistent with an Empathy score already at 1.8.

results.name: Waste Management
results.key_finding: Waste Management publishes real, benchmarked safety and emissions data and invests at scale, but the communities living next to its landfills reach it mainly through lawsuits, and the published 77.9 is a seed value shared byte-for-byte with ten unrelated companies.

results.name: Zoetis
results.key_finding: Zoetis reports a completed five-year sustainability cycle with specific, verifiable numbers — 29% lower emissions, 85% renewable electricity, 35 million dollars of Foundation grants — while its own employees describe a restructuring that they say destroyed the culture those numbers were meant to reflect.

results.name: SEI Investments
results.key_finding: SEI Investments settled a lawsuit alleging it made its own employees’ retirement plan a captive customer of its own funds for 6.8 million dollars, its most recent sustainability report is for 2023, and employee ratings of pay have fallen 12% in a year — the thinnest evidence base and the lowest measured score of the five rotation entities.

results.name: The Hartford
results.key_finding: The Hartford has the strongest internal culture evidence of the five rotation entities assessed tonight — 3.8 of 5 across 4,277 employee reviews with 72% recommending it — while a Florida regulator found failures in its hurricane claims handling and its group-disability offset practices are in class-action discovery.

results.name: Travelers
results.key_finding: Travelers does genuine structural work on whether people can get insured at all, and reports 24 million dollars of giving with 125,000 employee volunteer hours — but it has twice settled class actions over systematically paying claimants less than their policy limits.

withheld_on_attribution.rule: Attribution: TPS expiry is a United States immigration decision. No US policy charged to El Salvador. El Salvador’s own measurable conduct (public silence, no located reception plan) is already priced into the near-floor 15.0 set 2026-07-05 on the government’s own conduct.

Attribution: the ICE raid and the 2026-09-15 federal claim are US federal (ICE/DHS) conduct; Georgia is not a defendant and the governor was not notified in advance. Georgia’s own three documented actions were scored and are consistent with EMP 1.8 / EQU 1.6 already carried.

Non-institutional conduct: a researcher’s resignation and public speech is an individual’s conduct, not the institution’s. No upward movement taken on the absence of retaliation (screening rule 3). The one arguably institutional element (the alignment lead’s public concession of a missing plan) is already reflected in SYS 3.0 / INT 3.0 carried from 2026-09-15.

Allegation discipline (Netflix precedent): the 2026-09-14 Khalil/SIPA suit, the August 2026 Palestinian students and faculty suit, and the private-investigator claim are ALLEGATIONS and are not scored as findings. Every score-moving fact is a completed act, a regulator finding or a published agreement. The proposal would reach the same band if both suits were dismissed.

Pre-adjudication discipline: an active investigation is not yet a finding about conduct. Asset seizures (320.86m baht) and the 5,000 answer-sheet mismatches are scored as facts; culpability is not. The negative and positive readings offset and the net is zero.

calibration_findings.detail: All five rotation-backfill entities assessed tonight sit in identical-dimension-vector cohorts in site/src/data/indexes/fortune-500.json: Waste Management and Zoetis share a byte-identical vector (AWR/EMP/ACT/BND/ACC/SYS 4.0, EQU/INT 3.5, composite 77.9) with 9 other unrelated companies across unrelated sectors; SEI Investments, The Hartford and Travelers share a byte-identical vector (all dimensions 3.5 except EQU 3.0, composite 60.9) with 16 others. Byte-identical vectors across unrelated companies in unrelated sectors are the signature of unassessed seed values, not of measurement. First formal baselines measured tonight land at 46.3, 43.8, 31.3, 43.8 and 48.1 respectively — gaps of -31.6, -34.1, -29.6, -17.1 and -12.8. Per anti-false-positive screening rule 5, this is a cohort calibration problem and MUST NOT be resolved through five one-off baseline-reset proposals. No change proposals were filed. Full 40-subdimension measurements and sidecars are on disk for all five so a coordinator-level fortune-500 recalibration can use them.

calibration_findings.finding: global-cities seed markers (observation only, not the basis of any score move)
calibration_findings.detail: Seoul’s published 60.9 sits in a three-entity identical-vector cohort with Toronto and Vancouver. Amsterdam’s 94.4 vector is unique but is a near-uniform 4.5 with EQU and INT at 4.0, and places the city 8th of 250 in the Exemplary band, which the methodology defines as practices "independently verified, consistent, and sustained". Both proposals filed tonight rest on entity-specific Tier 4-5 evidence, NOT on this observation. The coordinator may wish to review whether other never-assessed Established and Exemplary band global cities carry the same overstatement.
